description: An oscillator giving a sine wave, a morphing wave that grows a spike out of that sine, and a square one octave down

params.text: Sets the pitch, from 10Hz at the far left to 10000Hz at the far right, and starts at 261.63Hz
Detunes the oscillator by up to a hundred cents either side of the pitch set by FREQ
Sets how much of the voltage at the LIN FM jack reaches the frequency, none at the far left
Grows a triangular spike out of the trough of the sine on the MORPH output, wider and taller the further it is turned; at the far left the MORPH output is a plain sine
Snaps FREQ to whole octaves above and below middle C instead of letting it run smoothly, and starts off
Sets how sharply the spike meets the sine around it, a soft join at the far left and a hard corner at the far right, and starts at the halfway point

inputs.text: Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, added to FREQ and FINE
Adds to the pitch at a volt per octave, with no attenuator of its own, so it does the same arithmetic as V/OCT
Modulates the frequency as a fraction of the current pitch, scaled by the LIN FM knob; the signal is stripped of any steady offset before it is used, so only its swing counts
Scales the MORPH knob rather than adding to it, reaching the full knob setting at 8V; while a cable is in this jack a voltage of 0V leaves the output a plain sine whatever the knob says
A rising edge above 1V restarts the waveform from the beginning of its cycle
A voltage above 1V lets the sub square run, and below that it holds the SUB output at 0V; with nothing patched the sub runs all the time

outputs.text: A sine wave at the pitch the module is set to, swinging ±5V
The sine with the spike grown out of it by MORPH, clamped to ±5V
A square wave one octave below the pitch the module is set to, swinging ±5V; it flips on each cycle of the main waveform

notes: the dark rectangle draws one cycle of the MORPH waveform as it is shaped; nothing on it can be clicked or dragged
menu: Coarse Tune: Continuous, Octave Stepped — the same choice the OCT button makes, between a freely swept FREQ knob and one that snaps to octaves
Asymmetry: Off, Rising, Falling — lifts one flank of the morph spike so the waveform is no longer symmetrical, on whichever side is chosen
Analog character — puts a soft, level-dependent saturation on the sine and morph outputs
Preview tracer — draws a moving marker on the waveform display showing where in the cycle the oscillator is
